Set as the always-on VPN in system settings.
Why Web Shield needs a VPN

Android lets an app see which websites the phone looks up only through a VPN. Web Shield uses that permission for one thing: before an app connects to a site, it checks the site against a list of known malware and phishing domains, on this phone.

• Only address lookups (DNS) pass through Web Shield. Your browsing itself goes straight to the internet, untouched.
• Nothing is sent to a VPN server. Allowed lookups go to the same resolver your network already uses.
• No browsing history is kept: only how many sites were blocked. An optional activity log of blocked sites stays on this phone.

Android will now ask you to allow the connection. A key icon shows while Web Shield is on.
